title: U.S. House · Illinois's 12th District
area: Southern Illinois, including Carbondale, Marion, and Mount Vernon.

context.text: Both candidates ran unopposed in their March 17, 2026 primaries: Mike Bost won the Republican primary with 100% (81,400 votes) and Julie Fortier won the Democratic primary with 100% (26,791 votes).

candidates.name: Mike Bost
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Mike Bost is the Republican U.S. Representative for Illinois's 12th District, first elected in 2014. He previously served six terms in the Illinois House of Representatives (1995-2014) and worked in his family's trucking business.

background.text: Born and raised in Murphysboro, Illinois; graduated Murphysboro High School in 1979.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1979 to 1982 as an electronic specialist and radar repairman, receiving an honorable discharge as a Corporal E-4.
Served on the Jackson County Board (1984-1988) and as Treasurer of Murphysboro Township (1989-1992).
Served six terms in the Illinois House of Representatives, District 115, from 1995 to 2014.

priorities.text: Says his plan for health care is to continue supporting the repeal of the Affordable Care Act and replace it with fiscally responsible, patient-centered reforms.
Says he is committed to maintaining the farm safety net established by the 2018 Farm Bill and reducing regulatory burdens on agriculture.
Says Washington must stop spending money it doesn't have and focus on creating opportunities for job growth.

positions.summary: Says he strongly supported the U.S. Supreme Court's decision overturning Roe v. Wade and has voted against what he calls the "pro-abortion agenda," and supports defunding Planned Parenthood.
positions.quote: I strongly supported the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision to overturn Roe v. Wade and restore the American people’s power to determine for themselves how abortion services are regulated in their state.

positions.summary: Says he will continue to support repealing the Affordable Care Act and has voted to repeal it and eliminate its individual and employer mandates.
positions.quote: This is why I will continue to support policies to repeal Obamacare and replace it with fiscally-responsible patient-centric reforms that help reduce costs without sacrificing access to care.

positions.summary: Opposes limiting fossil-fuel and coal use, saying he will push for an "all-of-the-above" energy policy against those who oppose any use of fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Unfortunately, despite the successes and benefits of these new technologies, there remain those opposed to any use of fossil fuels. A particular target has been coal.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the Committee on Agriculture (General Farm Commodities, Risk Management and Credit) and the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines).

candidates.name: Julie Fortier
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Julie Fortier is the Democratic nominee for Illinois's 12th Congressional District. She is a U.S. Air Force veteran.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Air Force.

researchNotes: No campaign website, public statements, or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey found for Julie Fortier beyond her Air Force service; positions and priorities could not be documented.
